text_fidelity_a:
Klutz Painted Rocks Craft Kit Multicolor, 10.5" Length x 0.75" Width x 8.5" Height This craft kit comes with a book on rock painting, eight acrylic paints, one paint brush, four pairs of self-adhesive googly eyes, and one rock. The kit is for ages 6 and up. The 40 page book comes with instructions on how to use the acrylic paints and included 28 step-by-step instructions for creating various paintings, from animals and flowers to various people, foods, and more. The book also contained pictures of other rock painting ideas but left it to the reader to figure out the steps needed to get the finished product. Most of these were pretty obvious and were similar to previous step-by-step projects.

The acrylic paints are white, black, blue, yellow, red, orange, green, and purple. Some of the designs required mixing these colors to make a new color, and adults may need to help younger kids with this. The paints had something in them to slow the drying time a little (so more like 30 minutes for dry to the touch rather than just a few minutes more typical for acrylic). This allowed for more time to make changes or mixing color on the rock.

The value in this kit is mainly the book as you only get one rock (thankfully...they're easy enough to get locally) and the painting supplies aren't going to go very far (maybe 10-20 rocks?). Still, this kit is enough to see if this is something your child enjoys. I painted the rock in the photo using the book instructions, but modifying the design to fit the rock.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Painted Rocks Craft Kit Multicolor, 10.5" Length x 0.75" Width x 8.5" Height

text_fidelity_a: Melissa & Doug Easel Accessory Set - Paint, Cups, Brushes, Chalk, Paper, Dry-Erase Marker I bought this accessory kit twice because I bought two Melissa and Dave easels for my grandson and twin granddaughters. You get everything that you need for your child to begin painting immediately. It comes with a sturdy roll of paper that fits nicely atop the M&D easel. The paper can also be used without the easel for painting, drawing and coloring.  It comes with bottles of paints in the primary colors which can easily be mixed to create other colors. The paint clean up is easy, but I still recommend a drop cloth under the easel. Since your child is sure to get paint on themselves, some soap and water will get it off quickly. The kit contains everything that your child needs to begin painting, except a drop cloth and an apron. Otherwise, you don't have to concern yourself with buying the items separately. I have texture issues especially with things that are grainy-ish(sand, Velcro, coke bottle lids, etc). This stuff was almost more than I could bear. My children did perfectly great with it, but they don't have texture sensitivities. *IF* your child does, then beware of this. Also, as you're playing with it, it feels stick-ish, like you'll need to wash your hands immediately, but once you stop touching it, all is well again. It's really odd stuff! ;)

Aside from that, it's really fun! My kids(2 and 5) love playing with it. There are quite a few molds included to make things such as cars and houses for the dinosaur to "stomp". As a momma of 3 little ones, it's one of those toys that will buy me some time to do one of the many things I have to do. I can put this on the table to occupy my oldest two and it will get me enough time to cook supper(or whatever).

Overall, we recommend this! My little ones have had a blast with it!

text_fidelity_a:
FurReal Friends Pax My Poopin Pup Plush Toy (Amazon Exclusive) I had high hopes for this little pooping doggo.. I purchased as a Christmas gift for my daughter (3 years old), who was obsessed with walking our dog and watching him pop (she’s a weirdo). Overall, she has gotten a fair amount of play and enjoyment out of the little fella, so I would *probably* purchase again.

Pros: He makes cute little doggy noises, he’s has soft fur.

Cons: He was much smaller than I expected (but my fault, as size is objective). He was overall much harder than I expected (other than his thin layer of fuzzy fur coat, he’s completely hard to the squeeze). He has wheels (which for some reason I thought he was more automatic than that). The leash is short (it was the perfect size for my tiny 3 year old when we bought it, but our 4 year old friend had to bend over to push it around). The treats / poo pellets are incredibly small. We lost a couple on christmas when we opened the gift.. and then a few more since. We have less than half left now (which I think is an accomplishment since we’ve had it almost a year!).

My toddler and her friends have enjoyed playing with it, but they have 1) been hurt by his hard material build (just minor boo boo, but still) 2) tried to eat the teeny pellet foods (cause, why not?) and 3) shoved other objects in its mouth that they weren’t supposed to. The design concept isn’t bad, but I do wish it was slightly bigger, with slightly bigger treats, a slightly longer leash, slightly more “squeezable”... you catch my drift. And with all that in mind, I probably would have gone with a different puppers.
text_fidelity_b: FurReal Friends Pax My Poopin Pup Plush Toy (Amazon Exclusive)

Super quiet brushless motors, 1 battery and usb charger, nice controller. Comes with decent quality carrying case that stores everything perfectly, along with a zippered compartment area, where you can keep the manuals and spare props, yes you get a set free with the drone!

Flies well in the wind I put it up in winds that were around 15-18 mph and it handled them well, of course the advertised battery life suffered and was only about 17 minutes but it was fighting the wind the whole time. On a less windy day it was almost 24 minutes of total flight time!

If your looking for a drone to learn on at a decent price point this is a good one and it's the right size, this is my 3rd Holy stone drone and I'm pleased with the product, I own the 700d, 270, and now this bad boy. All the features like follow me and point of interest work as expected I have yet too use way points on any of my birds, but the WiFi connection and FPV work well too.

I bought this one too go on Vacation with us in April to florida, mostly because of its footprint and portability, it is a little smaller than the 270.

Eventually I will be spending a ton on a DJI Mavic pro as I want to have a drone with autonomous flight and obstacle avoidance, but these drones have definitely exceeded my expectations and well worth the $$$ spent and are a great addition too my 7 other flying machines I have! So I highly recommend this unit!

Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition Ok, I have to start this review off by saying I had my reservations about this game. I absolutely love Euro strategy games like Puerto Rico, Agricola, Power Grid, Caylus, etc, but I'm not into card games. In fact, I pretty much hate card games.

This game was getting a lot of publicity on BoardGameGeek and everyone was raving about it so I decided that I should buy it to give it a shot. I'm glad I did.

The whole point of the game is to build your deck of cards and build up a collection of victory points. The reason this game shines is because it is a quick game that only takes about 30-40 minutes to play. It is also very fun because as you are building your deck of cards you aren't usually getting rid of the cards. If you spend some gold to buy a card that gold goes back into your discard pile and will eventually be shuffled for you to use again in another turn.

There are over 500 cards in this game with around 25 different action cards available so you can vary the game a lot depending on what cards are currently on the table. The only downside is that someone that has played the game a lot and knows a base strategy can usually beat a new player easily.

Overall this game is very addicting and short, which is a good thing. You can play multiple rounds of this game in an evening as opposed to one game of another typical Euro.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition

Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.

We used to mix up and pour our own plates for most of our plating and only used pre-made blood agar plates for growth isolation. That said, these EZ BioResearch Pre-poured Agar plates worked great for my child's science experiment. Though they were poured on the thin side, they were thick enough to show growth from water that had been filtered using various filtering devices. I was worried that they might dry out while being stored in the refrigerator until we were ready to use them, but they seemed fresh and clear of any contamination. The sterile swabs worked great for our purposes. The 10 plates and swabs gave us enough plates for two runs of our experiment plus controls.

I would definitely use these again. The nutrient agar was just what our bacteria wanted and these plates made it clear to us which filtering device was the best, and which one was the worst. Very good plates!

White Mountain Wacky Packages - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:bbf13e80bc0bb99a1834994a2f95588d]] I liked this puzzle. It's based on a print of compilation artwork by Charlie Girard, based on Topps' Wacky Packages trading cards. The puzzle contains dozens of pictures of these cards. An example is "Smoocher's Sticky Jam: for longer kisses," instead of Smucker's Jam. Another example is "Toad: Froggy's favorite for the cleanest frog in town. Bubble bath for toads," instead of Tide detergent.

This puzzle claims it's the World's Funniest Puzzle. I think that's a bit of an over-exaggeration, unless you're the type of person who really likes pranks like the snake in the nut can, shock candy bars, and whoopee cushions. This puzzle doesn't contain any of those classic gags, but that's the style of the humor in this print. And, it makes sense, because the Topps cards that this artwork is based on are from the 1960's and 1970's. Topps reissues them every year, but they're classic, older cards that are pictured in this puzzle.

The quality of this puzzle is awesome! The packaging is great. The pieces are big and sturdy, with high quality cardboard and a nicely-colored back. The pieces fit together snugly, so it's easy to tell if they fit or not. As you can see from my video, it's sturdy enough to pick up, which is rare in puzzles.

Pros:
+Excellent quality and manufacture
+Funny, old style humor
+Very nice pieces

Cons:
-Probably not actually the world's funniest puzzle
text_fidelity_b: White Mountain Wacky Packages - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Julius Jr. Rock 'n Playhouse Box Fisher Price knew what they were doing when they designed this Julius Jr. Rock'n Playhouse Box for ages 2 and up. The littlest children ages 2 and 3 years old just love it. The children really enjoy having Julius Jr. skateboard down the ramp and slide down the circular slide after going through a pie-shaped door.

They also love having Julius Jr. look through the telescope up on the rooftop and slide on the conveyor belt opening up the double doors where a Martian is ready for take-off in his space craft. But, their favorite thing is seeing the colorful dance floor light up and play music when Julius steps on it, as well as riding the elevator. There is even a disco ball attached to a weather vane upstairs that spins.

The elevator moves up to the second floor and rooftop, and with every floor, you hear Julius Jr. speak. He says things like, when he is looking out the window, What a beautiful day, I'm gonna need my sun hat. There are many sayings you will hear every time a bell rings at the floor stops, and they are different at times, so you will never know exactly what will be said.

This simple Playhouse is colorful and the pieces are made for little hands- easy to handle and nothing sharp. The Playhouse requires 2 AA batteries, which are included. You can also purchase extra Figure Packs, and you will want to, as Julius Jr. will have much more fun with a friend or two. Fisher Price has also made 2 more Playsets for Julius Jr. to play in- a Sortin' Sagebrush Farm and a Twirl-A-World Amusement Park. These sets will attach to this Playhouse making a world for Julius Jr. and your child to play in.

This 4 Star Rock'n Playhouse Box is a very simple set geared for the very young to enjoy with it's bright colors, sturdiness and simple moving parts. Two and three year olds especially love it.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Julius Jr. Rock 'n Playhouse Box

text_fidelity_a: Perplexus Rookie (Styles and Colors Vary) My 8 year old daughter received the Perplexus for Christmas, and our whole family fought over it for the rest of the holiday break.  My youngest turned four in early January, so I immediately ordered the Rookie version for him.  It arrived quickly, as we've become accustomed to when shopping Amazon, so ordering on December 27th for a January 2nd party was not a problem. It's been in my son's grubby little paws for five days  now and he is enamored of the thing.  It's wonderful to see my very large, very rough and tumble four year old boy carefully, slowly, cautiously navigate this little ball bearing around the maze.  He twist it, turns it, lifts it so he can see it from the bottom, and growls when the ball falls off the track.  But then he gets right back to it.  He has beaten it, but that doesn't seem to diminish his interest in trying again.  Whoever came up with this idea for this toy has my respect.  I only gave it four stars for durability because it seems like it could be a little higher quality.  For such an amazing toy, the materials should be of a high enough quality to make it an heirloom.  It is honestly one of my favorite toys, along with quadrilla and magnatiles, so I wish it was a little more substantial.  We have had no problems with it as of yet, though, after five days of heavy use.
text_fidelity_b: Perplexus Rookie (Styles and Colors Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
Lite-Brite Peg and Template Refill Pack, Light Up Drawing Board Accessories, LED Pegs with Colors, Toys for Creative Play, Light Toys for Kids Aged 4 + I had a light bright as a kid, it wasn't a favorite toy of mine but it was pretty invigorating - I might've used it only a couple of times. That thing seemed like a tank. I guess it had to be to protect the bulb. You could even buy a replacement bulb if it broke.

This one sadly feels a bit cold and inexpensively made. No glowing filament bulb to keep things warm. Nice, new energy efficient electronics that are powered by 3 AAA batteries - hopefully you have some rechargeable ones to use.

The kickstand is terrible. You either have to hold it or lay it flat to put the pegs in but even then it rocks side to side easily. When you use the kickstand a slight bump to the top of the unit could knock it over.

The bezel is also too wide and I also don't understand the reason for the extended parts of the black plastic on the side. With such a wide bezel you don't need them and it would like nicer as a square.

My unit does not glow evenly. I opened it to see if something wasn't working. Everything was but there just weren't enough lights, one more and a little adjustment would've helped. The unit is also on a timer. As it runs on batteries having it lit all the time would likely drain them. They should have added a USB port and just not included the cable. You're not able to keep it powered on 24/7. It's maybe a 10 minute timer. Pressing the button multiple times changes the light mode: lit, 3 section rotating flashing light show, full on off blink and the last one turns the 4 LEDs on 1 at a time and then off 1 at a time.

I made one of the provided examples and I had just enough pegs of a few colors. a few extras would been nice.

The sticker on mine was very crooked and out of place.

However, where the LEDs do light the unit right, it does look cool. I think, way better than the OG, they're more neon glow, the colors are much better, instead of a yellow glow the LEDs are bright white which allows you to have yellow, pink, orange, blue and white pegs. These colors on the dark background are nice.
The pegs stay in nicely. I've only made one picture but not one has fallen out. It may not hold up to repeated removing and placing of the pegs but I plan on leaving it with a certain design for a while.

This would be awesome if it just had a few improvements. I'd probably buy another

Hasbro, you can do better than this. For an MSRP of $19.99 it's not worth it. Even Amazon's marked down price is too high. This is something I'd expect to see at 5 and below.
text_fidelity_b: Lite-Brite Peg and Template Refill Pack, Light Up Drawing Board Accessories, LED Pegs with Colors, Toys for Creative Play, Light Toys for Kids Aged 4 +

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448) So....I'm Gen X and we played the original version some in college along with games like Risk and Stratego on weekends. It isnt quite a fluff game but it isnt very hard. I would think both children and adults would enjoy this game. A game adults can enjoy with their kids....or a fun starter game or game for chatting and having a beverage or three.

The best part is there is hardly any explanation needed to get started. Move tiles to open a path to get to the objects on your cards. And....block others from their goals. I love this game especially with 3 or 4 people instead of two. It requires some strategy but luck can make or break it, too.

Harry Potter version! Yes! Well...it is beautiful. The board looks wonderful! But in this version you are gathering "people" or characters rather than treasure items. The premise makes sense. Going through the maze that is Hogwarts gathering people ....you must match cards in your hands to pics on the tiles of the gameboard. Sounds AWESOME. In reality...it is kind of messy because some people look similar. Some people are the big characters...such as Harry or Snape....there were 3 I was like....who on earth is THIS and I thought I was a big fan. So....due to the pics on the game board being rather small....they are also color coded too. If your card is Harry with a blue border....Harry has a blue border on the game tile as well. But is there another character who looks very similar on the board with a blue border? Yes there is. So....yeah, it is really cool BUT pay good attention as the character pictures certainly are NOT as easy to discern as a scarab or diamond in the original. Hey...but it looks great!

I give this game 10 out of 10 because my gripes do not effect the game. If you are are a HP fan....and you already like or think you might like a labyrinth game...here ya go. This is 100% Ravensburg quality. The box is good quality as all the pieces. The box holds everything in the usual labyrinth organized way. Very nice.

At the price point....I really, really, really dont like wooden pegs. They are sort of big, bright and easy to move but I liked the Labyrinth version with the plastic characters NOT the one with wooden pegs. I have no idea WHY if your player piece coincides with a house....such as Slytherin....they didnt atleast make little plastic coats of armor for each house. I just hate generic pegs in fun games. But it doesnt make the game any better or worse. I saw some reviews where people complained about the card quality. It is the same it always has been. The cards are simply there to identify your next goal. This game doesnt require shuffling like Uno or slapping...or grabbing or swapping cards. They are perfectly fine.

Great game. Great Ravensburger quality. Dear Ravensburger.....I sure would love a Scooby Doo version with cool plastic player pieces!

I included pics and pics of game pieces from an earlier version of the original game
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448)

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3) This is one cool Mickey! In fact, he's so cool his "ice cream doesn't melt"! (one of his cheesy phrases, not mine) Seriously, this has to be one of the coolest toys ever. Not only do both of my boys(16 months and 3 3/4 years) like it, but my husband and I love him, too. Whenever we have visitors, we have to pull this Mickey out, just to show him off. Sad, but true. One day, my 11 year old nephew was over here, and he even commented that this is the "coolest Mickey ever", and his little brother has the original dancing Mickey. I'm not familiar with the other dancing Mickeys, but apparently this one has more features.

My only complaint is the batteries, which really can't be helped with the kind of toy it is. This is more of simply a warning for you than a complaint. This Mickey really sucks the power out of batteries! He takes 6 AA batteries. He does come with a set, but they will wear off REALLY quickly. I would definitely have a high quality set of batteries waiting nearby. When the batteries get low, he will keep moving, but he won't be able to do the really fancy moves, like the handstand, and leg spins. Those are my favorite, so it's disappointing when I don't get to see those. ;)

To make him dance, all you have to do is press his nose. He will only do one set of dance moves and then he will tell you if you want to see more, just press his nose. He turns off pretty quickly. I'm sure this is so he won't use up the batteries even quicker. I like that he's smart, too. When he falls over, he asks for help getting up. When you help him up, he says, Thanks, pal!". There is an on/off switch on the back of his head. I have to make use of this switch when my youngest takes a nap.

Overall, if you don't mind the big investment price and the many batteries he will require, we HIGHLY recommend this Mickey!
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3)

text_fidelity_a:
Avengers Marvel Legends Iron Man Electronic Helmet - Multicolor There are a few ways to evaluate this. I'll to approach it methodically.

Appearance
Nails it. Tony Stark could wear this. While it isn't metal, they got the color and the shape so spot-on. If you are looking for a piece to display in your home or office, this is it.

Size
This will fit all but the largest heads. M.O.D.O.K and The Watcher might not fit this, but almost everyone else will.

Weight
Not too heavy, but it weighs enough to feel real. It is comfortable.

Sounds
A weak spot. They sound much like greeting card special effects.

Lights
When the lights are on, it is hard to see. Cool, but nearly blinding. That means taking this to a con might be difficult.

Taking It On/Off
It is hard to explain, but it is tricky to get right. You can, so don't worry but be aware that undoing the back is a pain in the neck.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com
text_fidelity_b: Avengers Marvel Legends Iron Man Electronic Helmet - Multicolor

text_fidelity_a:
Paw Patrol, True Metal Adventure Bay Rescue Way Toy Playset with 2 Exclusive Die-Cast Vehicles, 1:55 Scale This Adventure Bay Rescue Way track is so much fun! This is the first race track in our house, and my toddler loves it. The yellow handle on the top pushes down to release the red stoppers on the blue ramps. The cars race down and then we do it all over again! There’s even a red flap on the track that the child can shift to a different position so the cars take a different path (there are 2 ramps with 3 route options). I do wish it had some minimal sound effects, like a "beep" button, or some rumble bumps on the track...something fun like that.

Assembly was easy overall. The hardest part for me was positioning the blue ramps. I thought I had placed them correctly, but then realized they needed to switch sides, which was my error. text_fidelity_a: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32" Purchased one of these without exactly knowing what I was buying. Sure, I knew it made noise - but didn't know how it did that or what it might sound like ( guess I could have looked on YouTube, but I didn't). Anyway, now that I've got one it's all everyone wants to play with. Basically it's a short tube with a thin piece of taut plastic covering one end (think tiny drum head), and a long loose spring mounted to the center of the plastic. Holding the tube and shaking it causes the spring to vibrate like springs do, those vibrations travel up to the drum head and the sound reverberates into the tube and is amplified out the other end. Makes for some pretty interesting sound effects. Overall I'm more than happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32"

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike Coming from a family of mostly boys and Big Wheel lovers, I know these current low riding Big Wheels are not the same quality as my little brother's Big Wheel from 1971. My brother loved his Big Wheel so much, that my son also had to have one when he was 3. Even though he was too small, he didn't care- walking it was just as good as riding it.

Things haven't changed much in the design, the big wheel bikes are all still too large for children under 4-5, but the quality has changed a lot for the original Big Wheel. After replacing the back seat 3 times, the original current Big Wheel of our nephew's recently went to the garbage. Replacing the Big Wheel with a tricycle was even worse- after a couple turns- the head injuries even with a helmet proved to be going from a cheap big wheel to bruises.

This Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is very similar to the Big Wheel of the seventies- very sturdy. The seat doesn't break at the pegs like the current Big Wheel. It is still too large for children under 5, but they don't care- they enjoy just having it, even if they have to walk it. They use their feet anyway for braking, so they don't mind walking it until their feet reach the pedals. My son walked his Big Wheel for a year before he could reach the pedals.

The best thing about this Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is our nephews love it. Taking the fastest high speed turns ends up in falls inches from the ground- meaning less painful minor injuries. My brother and son never had a bad injury being so close to the ground and this was in the days of no head protection. Putting it together was not difficult with the directions and once together, it's hard to keep the kids off. It's nice to see Radio Flyer keeping the tradition of making a sturdy Big Flyer that is perfect for 4 to 7 year olds, just like in the seventies when things were built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike

text_fidelity_a: MONOPOLY: Fortnite Edition Board Game Inspired by Fortnite Video Game Ages 13 & Up This version of Monopoly does not use money! Genius idea for very little children! Even my 4-year-old loved playing. It can be very quick (which was perfect!). I was out before I ever passed Go, haha. Instead of money, this game uses green circles called HP. You gradually lose them all to the “bank” in the middle, but you can get more by passing Go or by landing on a plus-one space or by drawing a particular card. When you land on an available property, it’s yours for free. If you land on an owned property, you have to pay a green HP. Simple. This game is easy to understand, super fun, and quick for the short attention spans of young Fortnite players. Instead of everyone starting on Go, we all started on a homemade Battle Bus, jumping off and landing on whatever space you want. So we all started the game in different areas of the board and all started with a property. That helped the game go faster and was just plain fun to copy Fortnite. My kids have already played this 5 times in 2 days. Great buy! I rate this board game A+.
text_fidelity_b: MONOPOLY: Fortnite Edition Board Game Inspired by Fortnite Video Game Ages 13 & Up

4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi This is a "dig kit", which I didn't realize when I got it. My oldest has a huge obsession with dinosaurs, and they are all his brain thinks about, so I thought a dinosaur DNA kit looked like something cool for him. It's really just a dig kit, though, with some added features that require a smart phone. Honestly, we just skipped all that, and used it as a simple dig kit. Even then, we'd already did a couple of them just before this one, so the whole digging process had become a little old for him.

Aside from that, it's an okay kit. The quality of the items to dig out usually aren't great, and this was no exception. My son has had trouble getting all the pieces to stick together as they should with all the dinosaur dig kits he's ever had, and again, this one was no exception. He became a little frustrated at some of the pieces.

If you've never used a dig kit before, they're messy! We've found them to be slightly less messy done inside a pie pan. Even so, outside is always better with these things(on a warm, windless day). Also, they require patience. This one wasn't near as hard to dig through as some of the other ones we've had, but it's definitely not the easiest, either. I'd say it's a medium level on hardness. It takes time to get all the pieces, and that's part of the process. It teaches a young person a bit of what it's like for archaeologists. If they rush the dig, they end up damaging pieces.

Overall, this is a fun little lesson in patience, for both children and adults, but it wasn't quite what I was expecting.

text_fidelity_a: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad The power wheels kawasaki lil' quad is a great toy for a toddler. You will want to make sure that your little one has enough flat space to drive around because the turning radius is extremely wide. You will need a very large space to make a complete circle. Also, there is no reverse button. You should not ride this near hills, slopes, pools, roads, cars, or anywhere else that could increase the chances of an accident. You should also note that even if the "go" button is not being pressed the quad can reach high speeds if on a steep incline.  It comes with a rechargeable 6v 4Ah battery and charging cord that is to be plugged into a wall outlet (not a ceiling outlet!). Before using for the first time the battery must be charged for 18 hours, and 14 hours after each use. You are warned not to leave the battery charging for longer than 30 hours or it may cause the battery to degrade. The biggest downside is that there is no light to denote the battery is charging or completely charged. You just have to assume it is charging and that the battery is completely charged after you unplug it. It requires about 10 minutes of assembly time (excluding the sticker time). The quad does not come with the stickers already placed, so you will need to place the stickers on yourself. You will need a philips head and a flat head screw driver, all other parts are included. The only problem that I noted was one of the connections would not completely engage. There is a wire that is used to connect the battery one end and then the electrical supply from the "go" but on the handlebar. For some reason I could not get the handlebar connection to completely snap into place. Even though it did not completely connect it was enough for everything to work, so I left it as is. I was afraid to force it to completely connect and potentially breaking the plastic connector. It is listed to be for 12-36 months, and up to 40 pounds. Personally, I think 12 months is a little young to be riding this, especially if your child is on the small side and not completely steady on their feet when walking. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad
